programs.name: BSF Research Grant Program (IDEA & DEVELOPMENT Grants)
programs.amount: IDEA up to $50,000 (1–2 yrs); DEVELOPMENT up to $100,000 (2–3 yrs)
programs.desc: BSF's grant program for Barth-specific research: seed grants for basic, translational, and clinical research on BTHS — natural history, biochemical basis, and treatment — intended to generate preliminary data for follow-on NIH-scale funding. Indirects are capped at 10%. Young/non-tenured investigators may put up to 75% of funds toward PI salary. Research-participant travel for clinical studies is budgeted outside the cap. BSF affiliates (Canada, UK/Barth Syndrome Trust, Barth Italia, Association Barth France) co-fund through this single program.
programs.eligibility: Independent investigators with faculty appointments, worldwide — no geographic restrictions. Postdocs cannot apply as PI (they are directed to the AHA/BSF co-funded fellowships instead).
programs.apply: Apply via BSF's SurveyMonkey Apply portal. An LOI is required for DEVELOPMENT-grant applications and optional for IDEA grants. Annual cycle: opens ~July 31, full applications due Oct 31, awards announced ~March. Guidelines, budget table, and grant policies are downloadable inside the portal. Contacts: Lindsay Marjoram, PhD, Director of Research (lindsay.marjoram@barthsyndrome.org); applications: Melissa Huang, PhD (melissa.huang@barthsyndrome.org).

programs.name: BSF Strategic Initiatives Program (SIP)
programs.deadline: No open call — initiated with BSF
programs.desc: Funding outside the competitive grant cycle for translational and clinical BTHS programs facing a specific technical, manufacturing, regulatory, or financial obstacle. Funded projects include the Collaborative Clinical Registry arrhythmia project (Tan/Phoon, NYU) and optimization of BTHS gene therapy capsids (William Pu, Boston Children's).
programs.eligibility: Investigators whose translational/clinical BTHS programs face a defined obstacle. There is no open competition; projects are coordinated with BSF.
programs.apply: No standing application cycle. Contact BSF's Director of Research (lindsay.marjoram@barthsyndrome.org) to discuss a project.

programs.name: AHA Predoctoral & Postdoctoral Fellowships (BSF co-funded)
programs.sponsor: American Heart Association + Barth Syndrome Foundation
programs.desc: AHA fellowships with BSF as a named co-funding partner: BSF designates collaboration money for meritorious applications focused on Barth syndrome and/or cardiolipin. BSF's own grants exclude pre- and postdocs; it directs trainees to this program. Predoc awards typically run 1–2 years; postdoc awards run 2 years on the NIH salary scale plus project support and travel.
programs.eligibility: AHA rules: research must be at a US institution; AHA membership required. Predoc: enrolled PhD/MD students. Postdoc: doctoral degree holders in training. Most AHA programs are not citizenship-restricted.
programs.apply: Apply through AHA's Grants@Heart system and indicate the BTHS/cardiolipin focus for co-funding consideration. The 2027-cycle deadlines were Aug 4 (predoc) and Aug 5, 2026 (postdoc); the 2028 cycle is expected ~summer 2027. AHA's broader portfolio (Career Development Award, Transformational Project Award) also funds pediatric cardiomyopathy research. Questions: apply@heart.org.

programs.name: UMDF Research Grant Program
programs.sponsor: United Mitochondrial Disease Foundation (with Mito Foundation)
programs.amount: Grad $25K/1 yr; postdoc $50K/2 yrs; PI $100K/2 yrs
programs.desc: Grants for any primary mitochondrial disease — Barth syndrome qualifies (2026 priority areas were mtFAS disorders, single large-scale mtDNA deletions, and Leigh syndrome; BTHS was eligible but not priority). Three career-stage tiers from graduate student to PI. The 2026 cycle, run jointly with Australia's Mito Foundation, awarded $500,000 across 8 grants. No indirect costs allowed.
programs.eligibility: Graduate students, postdocs, and PIs worldwide — international applicants welcome. One application per lab.
programs.apply: Full proposal (no LOI stage) via UMDF's SM Apply portal. The 2026 cycle ran Feb 2 – Mar 2, 2026 with awards in June; expect a similar window ~Feb 2027. Questions: grants@umdf.org.

programs.name: Mito Foundation Incubator & Major Annual Grants
programs.amount: Incubator up to A$25,000/12 mo; Major up to US$500,000
programs.desc: Two mechanisms open to researchers anywhere: Incubator Grants for early-stage, innovative primary mitochondrial disease projects (the 2026 round funded 4 projects starting Jul–Oct 2026), and the Major Annual Grant Program for high-impact translational and clinical-trial-readiness research (the 2026 round ran with UMDF).
programs.eligibility: Explicitly open to Australian and overseas researchers.
programs.apply: Apply via mito.org.au when rounds open; Incubator rounds recur annually.

programs.name: MDA Research & Development Grants — paused for 2026
programs.deadline: New cycles paused; possible targeted RFAs late 2026
programs.desc: Barth syndrome is on MDA's covered-disease list under metabolic diseases of muscle, and MDA historically funded Research Grants (~$100K/yr up to 3 yrs) and postdoc Development Grants. MDA announced it will not open a new Research or Development Grant cycle in 2026 (a budget-driven pause). It continues $17M+ in multi-year grants from prior cycles, still offers Conference Grants, and may issue targeted RFAs later in the year if funds allow.
programs.eligibility: Historically academic investigators and postdocs at nonprofit institutions working on MDA-covered diseases.
programs.apply: MDA maintains a grants mailing list (grants@mdausa.org); targeted RFAs or a resumed cycle would be posted on the funding-opportunities page.

programs.name: AFM-Téléthon Scientific Call for Proposals
programs.amount: Trampoline up to €50,000/1 yr; project grants; postdoc fellowships
programs.desc: Neuromuscular disease research funding; BTHS skeletal myopathy falls under the metabolic-diseases-of-muscle scope. Routes include Trampoline grants (early-stage/higher-risk, up to €50,000), 1-year research project grants, and renewable postdoctoral fellowships.
programs.eligibility: International — open to French and foreign teams.
programs.apply: The 2026 call ran Feb 3 – Mar 10, 2026; the annual call recurs ~February. Apply via the AFM-Téléthon calls page.

programs.name: NORD Seed Grant Program (no BTHS fund yet)
programs.desc: NORD runs disease-specific seed-grant RFPs funded by donor/patient-organization restricted funds, awarded on merit by its Medical Advisory Committee. No Barth syndrome RFA currently exists or has historically; one would appear only if BSF or donors seeded a restricted fund with NORD.
programs.eligibility: Academic scientists internationally, including early-career, applying under whichever disease-specific RFAs are posted.
programs.apply: The annual RFP announcement is posted ~August. A Barth-specific RFA would require BSF or donors to establish a restricted fund with NORD.

programs.name: Million Dollar Bike Ride Pilot Grants (requires a Barth team)
programs.amount: Team fundraising + Penn match up to $30K
programs.deadline: Next ride June 2027 at earliest for a new team
programs.desc: Disease communities field fundraising teams at the annual ride; the Orphan Disease Center then administers a one-year pilot-grant RFP per participating disease, sized to that team's fundraising plus a Penn match. No Barth syndrome team has participated to date; a BTHS RFP would exist only if BSF or families fielded a team, after which BTHS researchers anywhere could apply.
programs.eligibility: Researchers apply to disease-specific RFPs (LOI then invited full application); a disease qualifies by fielding a ride team.
programs.apply: A Barth RFP would require BSF or families to register a team for the next ride; any resulting RFP would be posted on the ODC grants page.

programs.name: Pediatric Cardiomyopathy Registry Collaboration (grants discontinued)
programs.desc: CCF no longer offers research grants (a strategy shift after funding grants 2002–2019). It now funds a prospective Pediatric Cardiomyopathy Patient Registry and multi-center studies building on the NIH-funded North American Pediatric Cardiomyopathy Registry, and takes collaboration inquiries. For BTHS cardiomyopathy studies it is a data/cohort resource rather than a funder.
programs.eligibility: Clinical researchers seeking registry collaboration.
programs.apply: Email info@childrenscardiomyopathy.org with a collaboration proposal.

programs.name: Genetic Alliance Infrastructure (IRB, PEER registry, BioBank)
programs.desc: Infrastructure for advocacy-led research: a low-cost independent IRB specialized in registries, natural-history studies, and surveys (roughly 15x faster turnaround than academic IRBs; a SMART IRB founding member); the PEER/Luna registry and data-collection platform with participant-controlled sharing; and a cooperative BioBank where member organizations run their own collections at negotiated rates. BSF's registry and any advocacy-led BTHS study needing IRB review fall within this scope.
programs.eligibility: Any disease advocacy organization; cooperative membership model.
programs.apply: IRB: irbadmin@geneticalliance.org. PEER/BioBank: through the program pages.

programs.name: RARE-X Data Collection Program
programs.desc: Patient-owned data-collection infrastructure — structured surveys, patient-reported outcomes, cross-condition analysis — delivered in partnership with advocacy groups (85+ disorders, 124 partner groups, participants in 90+ countries; methods published in Genetics in Medicine, 2025). A researcher data-request process makes collected data usable for BTHS studies.
programs.eligibility: Rare disease patient advocacy organizations become data-collection partners; researchers can submit data requests.
programs.apply: Program inquiry via the Global Genes RARE-X pages; researchers use the data-request form.

programs.name: Global Genes Advocate Travel Support
programs.amount: Up to $800 domestic / $1,200 international per advocate
programs.desc: Travel assistance (flights, ground transport, hotel, meals) for in-person attendance at Global Genes events — the RARE Advocacy Summit, RARE Drug Development Symposium, and Week in RARE. First-time recipients are prioritized. Covers attendance costs for BSF staff and community members at advocacy and drug-development training events.
programs.eligibility: Rare disease advocates; individual application per event; funds contingent on sponsor participation.
programs.apply: Apply through each event's advocate-support page.

programs.name: Workplace Giving & Credibility Infrastructure
programs.amount: Passive donation channels; free transparency seals
programs.desc: Donation and transparency infrastructure for nonprofits. Registering free on Benevity Causes (plus YourCause and CyberGrants FrontDoor) opens employee donations and corporate matching from hundreds of large employers. Claiming the Candid nonprofit profile earns transparency seals; seal-holders average 62% more in contributions, and some funders require a seal as an eligibility gate. The highest tiers are Gold and Platinum.
programs.eligibility: Verified 501(c)(3) with banking/electronic disbursement set up.
programs.apply: Register on the Benevity Causes portal; claim and complete the Candid profile.

programs.name: Milken Institute SPARC (philanthropy advisory)
programs.desc: Not a grantmaker; there is no application. SPARC advises philanthropists and family foundations on designing rare-disease research giving, and administers donor-funded grant programs (the Kissick Family Foundation FTD program, the ALS Breakthrough Research Fund) plus landscape analyses. A major donor interested in Barth syndrome could engage SPARC to design and run a BTHS research fund.
programs.eligibility: Engagement-based; no application cycle exists.
programs.apply: Contact sparc@milkeninstitute.org; engagements typically arise around a specific major donor or a proposed landscape analysis.

programs.name: NIH Parent R01 (PA-25-301 / PA-25-305)
programs.amount: Uncapped (>$500K/yr direct needs IC approval), up to 5 years
programs.deadline: Feb 5, Jun 5, Oct 5 (new); active through Jan 2028
programs.desc: NIH's standard investigator-initiated mechanism for basic and translational research, covering TAFAZZIN biology, cardiolipin remodeling, and cardiomyopathy/neutropenia/myopathy mechanisms. Participating institutes include NHLBI (cardiomyopathy), NINDS, NIAMS (skeletal muscle), NICHD, NIGMS, and NCATS (from Jul 2026 due dates). Two variants: Clinical Trial Not Allowed (PA-25-301) and Clinical Trial Required (PA-25-305).
programs.eligibility: Academic institutions, nonprofits, for-profits, and governments; foreign organizations eligible (foreign subawards prohibited under the current announcement). Any career stage with a PI-eligible appointment.
programs.apply: Electronic submission via eRA Commons / Grants.gov / ASSIST with your institution's grants office. Standard due dates Feb 5, Jun 5, Oct 5; renewals/resubmissions Mar 5, Jul 5, Nov 5.

programs.name: NIH Parent R21 & R03 (exploratory / small grants)
programs.desc: R21 funds high-risk exploratory projects ($275K direct total over 2 years, max $200K in one year), including new BTHS models, biomarker pilots, and mechanism-testing studies. R03 funds small discrete projects. NHLBI, NINDS, NIAMS, NICHD, and NCATS participate in the parent R21; NIGMS does not. R03 participation varies by institute and is listed on IC pages.
programs.eligibility: Same broad eligibility as the R01; foreign organizations eligible for the R21.
programs.apply: Via eRA Commons / Grants.gov / ASSIST under the current parent announcements; standard due dates Feb 16, Jun 16, Oct 16.

programs.name: NCATS Preclinical Proof of Concept Studies for Rare Diseases (R21)
programs.desc: Funds efficacy studies of a proposed therapeutic in an established rare-disease model (PK/PD allowed) to justify further development toward IND. TAFAZZIN gene therapy, mitochondria-targeted agents, and cardiolipin-targeted candidates in tafazzin-KO models are within scope. Roughly 3–5 awards per year.
programs.eligibility: US higher-education institutions, nonprofits, for-profits, and governments. Domestic only — no foreign components or subawards.
programs.apply: Via eRA Commons / Grants.gov / ASSIST under RFA-TR-25-002; the deadline was extended to Jun 2, 2027.

programs.name: Clinical Trial Readiness for Rare Diseases (R21)
programs.sponsor: NCATS + NICHD / Office of Rare Diseases Research (PAR-25-450)
programs.desc: Funds development and validation of biomarkers, clinical outcome assessments, and natural-history data needed before a rare-disease trial. BTHS-applicable endpoints include cardiac function measures, functional outcomes, and the monolysocardiolipin/cardiolipin ratio as a biomarker.
programs.eligibility: US institutions of all types; foreign organizations ineligible. Applicants need clinical expertise in the disease and access to sufficient patients; BSF's registry and clinics are relevant resources.
programs.apply: Via eRA Commons / Grants.gov / ASSIST under PAR-25-450; Feb/Jun cycles through 2028, next due date Feb 17, 2027.

programs.name: Rare Diseases Clinical Research Network — NAMDC collaboration
programs.sponsor: NCATS RDCRN / North American Mitochondrial Disease Consortium
programs.desc: The RDCRN funds multi-site consortia for natural history, biomarker, and trial-readiness research. The North American Mitochondrial Disease Consortium (NAMDC) is an active cycle-5 consortium with a registry, biorepository, and 17 clinical sites. The new-consortium NOFO has expired, with the next competition expected ~2029; in the interim, access runs through affiliation or collaboration with NAMDC, which sometimes offers pilot awards within the consortium.
programs.eligibility: Clinical and translational investigators in mitochondrial disease seeking multi-site infrastructure, registry, or biorepository access.
programs.apply: Contact NAMDC/RDCRN directly to discuss affiliation, data/sample access, or pilot opportunities.

programs.name: NCATS TRND & BrIDGs (in-kind preclinical development)
programs.sponsor: NCATS Division of Preclinical Innovation, NIH
programs.desc: Collaborative programs providing in-kind drug-development services — lead optimization, IND-enabling toxicology, GMP formulation, and regulatory support — to bring a rare-disease therapeutic to IND. The track record includes FDA-approved rare-disease products. Services that would otherwise be contracted to CROs are provided at no cost.
programs.eligibility: Academic labs, nonprofits, and companies, via collaboration agreements.
programs.apply: Engage the Therapeutic Development Branch at askTDB@nih.gov or via the program pages; proposals are taken on a rolling basis.

programs.name: FDA Orphan Products Grants — Clinical Trials (RFA-FD-25-020)
programs.sponsor: FDA Office of Orphan Products Development
programs.amount: Up to $650K/yr × 4 yrs ($900K/yr for innovative designs)
programs.desc: Funds phase 1–3 clinical trials of drugs, biologics, devices, or medical foods for rare diseases to support new indications or labeling. BTHS trials, including follow-ons to elamipretide-class programs or gene therapy, are within scope; FDA has previously funded BTHS-relevant orphan trials.
programs.eligibility: Domestic and foreign applicants, academic or industry — any organization able to conduct the trial (the product must not yet be approved for the indication).
programs.apply: NIH-style R01 application to FDA via Grants.gov / eRA Commons. Next receipt date Oct 20, 2026.

programs.name: FDA Orphan Products Grants — Natural History Studies (RFA-FD-25-017)
programs.sponsor: FDA Office of Orphan Products Development
programs.amount: Prospective up to $400–600K/yr × 4 yrs; retrospective $150K/yr × 2 yrs
programs.desc: Funds protocol-driven natural history studies that support product development — relevant to extending BTHS natural-history and registry data toward regulatory-grade endpoints.
programs.eligibility: Domestic and foreign applicants, academia and industry.
programs.apply: Via Grants.gov / eRA Commons under RFA-FD-25-017. The Feb 10, 2026 receipt date has passed; the next is Feb 8, 2028.

programs.name: Orphan Drug & Rare Pediatric Disease Designations (incentives)
programs.sponsor: FDA Office of Orphan Products Development
programs.amount: 7-yr exclusivity, 25% trial tax credit, fee waiver, PRV
programs.deadline: Rolling, no fee; PRV program runs through Sept 2029
programs.desc: Regulatory incentives rather than grants. Orphan Drug Designation brings 7-year marketing exclusivity, a 25% tax credit on qualified clinical trial costs, PDUFA fee waiver, and eligibility for the FDA orphan grants; BTHS meets the prevalence threshold. The Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher program was reauthorized in Feb 2026 through September 2029: a sponsor winning approval of a BTHS therapy can receive a transferable voucher, and recent vouchers have sold for more than $100M.
programs.eligibility: Drug/biologic sponsors — companies or academic sponsors of INDs.
programs.apply: Designation requests go to OOPD on a rolling basis (no fee, no deadline) via FDA's designation request forms.

programs.name: DoD Peer Reviewed Medical Research Program (PRMRP)
programs.sponsor: Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs, Dept. of Defense
programs.amount: Up to ~$5.6M (TTDA); clinical trial awards to $20M
programs.deadline: FY26 pre-apps closed Jul 23, 2026; FY27 cycle ~summer 2027
programs.desc: Mitochondrial Disease is one of 69 FY26 PRMRP topic areas designated by Congress as military health priorities, so Barth syndrome qualifies on topic. FY26 mechanisms include the Technology/Therapeutic Development Award (~$5.6M total costs), Clinical Trial Award ($6M–$20M funding levels), and Impact Award, from a $370M appropriation.
programs.eligibility: Academic, industry, government, and military investigators worldwide — no citizenship restriction. Applications must address a listed topic area (Mitochondrial Disease) and include a one-page Military Relevance Statement.
programs.apply: Two-step process: pre-application via eBRAP, then full application via Grants.gov. FY26 pre-applications closed Jul 23, 2026 (Clinical Trial Award full applications due Sept 22, 2026 for those with pre-applications in); the FY27 cycle is expected ~summer 2027, assuming mitochondrial disease remains a topic area. Applications must include a one-page Military Relevance Statement covering disease prevalence in service members, veterans, and beneficiaries, and dual-use benefit — how the knowledge gained serves both civilian and military needs. Relevant facts for BTHS: military families are TRICARE beneficiaries and affected boys are covered dependants (the Exceptional Family Member Program covers this population); and Barth syndrome is a human model of isolated cardiolipin deficiency, so findings bear on mitochondrial dysfunction in blast injury and TBI (Brain Injury Impact on Cardiac Health is a separate FY26 topic area), Gulf War Illness, exertional rhabdomyolysis and heat illness, and ischemia-reperfusion after hemorrhage. Elamipretide was studied in ischemia-reperfusion before Barth syndrome.

programs.name: NIH SBIR / STTR (small business therapeutics development)
programs.deadline: First receipt Sept 8, 2026; then Jan 5 & Apr 5, 2027
programs.desc: Small-business-led development of BTHS therapeutics and diagnostics — gene therapy, mitochondria-targeted drugs, cardiolipin-ratio diagnostics. Rare-disease therapeutics is a stated NIH SBIR priority area, and several institutes fund above standard caps for approved waiver topics. STTR requires a nonprofit research-institution partner, which accommodates academic labs spinning out companies.
programs.eligibility: US small businesses (<500 employees, majority US-owned); STTR requires a nonprofit research-institution partner.
programs.apply: Via eRA Commons / Grants.gov under the FY26 series (reposted Jun 1, 2026). First receipt date Sept 8, 2026, then standard cycles Jan 5 and Apr 5, 2027.

programs.name: NHLBI Catalyze Program (translational product development)
programs.desc: Preclinical product development for heart, lung, and blood conditions — relevant for a BTHS cardiomyopathy or neutropenia therapeutic. Two arms: grant NOFOs such as RFA-HL-26-017 (Product Definition R61/R33, target ID/validation through lead series), and Catalyze Preclinical Services delivering CRO/CMO IND-enabling work in kind.
programs.eligibility: Academic and small-business investigators; the services arm requires an Expression of Interest and milestone agreements.
programs.apply: Grants via eRA Commons / Grants.gov (see the RFA); services via an EOI at nhlbicatalyze.org — the next window is Sept 14 – Oct 2, 2026.

programs.name: ERDERA Joint Transnational Calls (Europe + partners)
programs.sponsor: European Rare Diseases Research Alliance (Horizon Europe)
programs.desc: The successor to EJP RD runs annual joint transnational calls with rotating themes across ~35 countries (NIH participates in some calls). The 2026 call targeted undiagnosed cases and has closed; that theme did not cover BTHS, but earlier themes such as preclinical therapy development did. The JTC 2027 theme has not been announced.
programs.eligibility: Consortia of 4–6 PIs from at least 4 participating countries, each funded by their national agency; US PIs can join when NIH/NCATS participates.
programs.apply: Two-stage (pre-proposal then full) via the ERDERA electronic submission system when the call opens.

programs.name: UK MRC Applicant-Led Research Grants
programs.amount: Typically up to ~£1M over 3–5 years (80% FEC)
programs.deadline: Rolling — no closing dates since Apr 2026
programs.desc: Investigator-initiated biomedical research including rare-disease mechanisms and translation; the Molecular & Cellular Medicine board covers mitochondrial biology. Since April 2026, applicant-led opportunities are open with no closing dates under MRC's flexible research grant.
programs.eligibility: UK-based research organizations; international co-investigators allowed.
programs.apply: Submit anytime via the UKRI Funding Service.

programs.name: CIHR Project Grant Program
programs.desc: Canada's open investigator-initiated program covering any health research including rare disease. Competitions run twice yearly (spring/fall). CIHR also runs a Rare Disease Research Initiative with its own opportunities.
programs.eligibility: Independent researchers at eligible Canadian institutions.
programs.apply: Via ResearchNet: Fall 2026 registration closes Aug 12, 2026, applications Sept 9, 2026, decisions ~Jan 2027.

programs.name: PCORI Eugene Washington Engagement Awards
programs.amount: Up to $300,000 by track; small-orgs track up to $250,000
programs.desc: Non-research awards building capacity for patient-centered comparative effectiveness research — up to $25M available in FY2026 across four tracks: Capacity Building (≤$300K/2 yrs), Dissemination (≤$300K), Convening Support (≤$125K, applicable to BSF's biannual conference), and Building Capacity for Small Organizations (≤$250K, restricted to organizations with ≤$1.5M average operating budget, a cap BSF falls under; includes a peer learning network).
programs.eligibility: US-based organizations; patient advocacy nonprofits explicitly eligible. This funds engagement capacity, not research itself.
programs.apply: Two cycles per year: Letter of Intent, then invited full proposal via the PCORI Connect portal. Fall 2026: LOIs due Oct 1, 2026, full proposals Jan 11, 2027. Contact: ea@pcori.org.

programs.name: NIH R13 Conference Grants (PA-25-080)
programs.amount: Typically $10K–$50K/yr; up to 5 years for recurring series
programs.desc: Cash support for scientific conferences and workshops, including the scientific sessions of BSF's biannual conference; a recurring series run by a permanent sponsoring organization can receive up to 5 years of support. Effective Feb 10, 2026, NIH no longer requires advance institute permission for conference grant applications (NOT-OD-26-040).
programs.eligibility: Nonprofits with or without 501(c)(3) status are explicitly eligible, alongside universities and governments. Requires eRA Commons/SAM.gov registration; patient organizations can apply directly or co-sponsor with an academic partner.
programs.apply: Via Grants.gov/ASSIST under PA-25-080 (or its successor) at standard NIH due dates.

programs.name: FORZINITY (elamipretide) — EAP, Phase IV sites & investigator studies
programs.amount: Drug supply, trial-site participation, case-by-case IIS support
programs.desc: FORZINITY received FDA accelerated approval Sept 19, 2025 — the first approved therapy for Barth syndrome (adults and children ≥30 kg) and the first mitochondria-targeted therapeutic. Three researcher/clinician touchpoints: the Expanded Access Program continues drug supply for patients who cannot access it via approval or trials (including <30 kg patients previously enrolled); a Phase IV confirmatory study is enrolling BTHS clinical sites, with the first patient dosed in 2026; and investigator-initiated studies have precedent (an elamipretide IIS at CHOP), with drug supply negotiated case by case through medical affairs. Stealth BioTherapeutics became Mighty Therapeutics in ~June 2026.
programs.eligibility: EAP: treating physicians of patients with serious mitochondrial disease and no comparable alternative. IIS: qualified academic investigators, case by case. Phase IV: BTHS clinical sites.
programs.apply: EAP: email EAP@mightytx.com and complete the Patient Information Intake Form (emergency line 617-600-6888). IIS and site-participation requests go to medical affairs via info@mightytx.com or the contact page; rolling.

programs.name: Alexion Externally Sponsored Research
programs.desc: Funding and/or drug for investigator-initiated rare-disease studies — interventional, non-interventional, or preclinical — complementing Alexion's portfolio. Stated focus areas include metabolic disorders, cardiology, hematology, and neurology. Proposals must align with Alexion's strategic interests; BTHS work would fall under the metabolic or cardiology areas.
programs.eligibility: Qualified external academic investigators and clinicians; the study is initiated and managed by the investigator, independent of Alexion.
programs.apply: Submit an unsolicited proposal through Alexion's ESR online process; rolling.

programs.name: Pfizer Investigator Sponsored Research
programs.deadline: Batched review cycles (windows posted on site)
programs.desc: Funding and/or drug for investigator-sponsored preclinical and clinical studies involving a Pfizer asset, plus general research projects. Rare-disease areas include ATTR cardiac amyloidosis / rare cardiomyopathy (tafamidis). Pfizer has no active rare-DCM asset; a BTHS proposal would need to connect to the rare-cardiomyopathy areas, for example heart-failure phenotyping methodology.
programs.eligibility: Qualified researchers at eligible institutions; country lists apply per therapeutic area.
programs.apply: Via the Pfizer ISR portal (pfizer.com/ISR); applications are reviewed in batched cycles published on the site, with contracting targeted within 60 days of approval.

programs.name: Bristol Myers Squibb Investigator Sponsored Research
programs.amount: Funding and/or drug via posted RFPs
programs.desc: BMS has moved from rolling submissions to an RFP model with defined areas of interest, including cardiovascular (the mavacamten/Camzyos cardiac-myosin franchise in HCM). A BTHS skeletal/cardiac muscle physiology proposal is eligible only if a current RFP's scope covers inherited cardiomyopathy phenotyping.
programs.eligibility: External investigators responding to posted RFPs; a profile and CV are required in the portal.
programs.apply: Register in the FastTrack Investigator Portal and respond to a matching RFP from the competitive research grants listing.

programs.name: iHope Genetic Health (no-cost clinical genome sequencing)
programs.amount: In-kind WGS/WES + reagents, cloud storage, software
programs.deadline: Rolling site applications; patient referral via network sites
programs.desc: A $120M initiative providing no-cost clinical whole-genome sequencing for undiagnosed children with suspected genetic disease, applicable to suspected-BTHS diagnostic confirmation and cohort building. Over 1,000 patients/year across 25 clinical sites in 14 countries; partner labs receive in-kind flow cells, reagents, library prep, cloud storage, and software. PacBio joined in Feb 2026, adding HiFi long-read WGS. Administered by Genetic Alliance (Illumina is founding sponsor); applications go to Genetic Alliance, not Illumina.
programs.eligibility: Clinical sites and labs serving under-resourced communities, with priority for rare-disease/pediatrics/genetics experience; clinicians refer patients through member sites.
programs.apply: Clinical sites apply via the site-engagement page (rolling review); clinicians route patients through existing network sites.

programs.name: PacBio SMRT Grant Programs
programs.desc: Free long-read sequencing — consumables, library prep, Revio sequencing, and initial bioinformatics via certified service providers — through continually running themed grant rounds plus local/regional SMRT grants. Rounds relevant to BTHS (rare disease / human genetics themes) appear periodically; the application is a 100-word proposal.
programs.eligibility: Scientists at any level; short-form application.
programs.apply: Themed windows are posted on the SMRT Grant page; the application is the short proposal, and decisions come ~2 months from submission.

programs.name: Free Genetic Testing for Mitochondrial Disease
programs.amount: Free at-home WGS (incl. mtDNA) + genetic counseling
programs.deadline: Rolling — verify current status before relying on it
programs.desc: Patient-initiated free whole-genome sequencing with genetic counseling for US patients with suspected mitochondrial disease, applicable to BTHS case-finding and diagnosis. The mito-specific portal still exists, but the current sponsor and 2026 program status could not be verified; confirmation is needed before citing the program as active.
programs.eligibility: US patients and families, initiated via a symptom questionnaire with physician follow-up.
programs.apply: Through the Probably Genetic mito portal or UMDF's genetic testing page.

programs.name: Charles River rare-disease collaborations
programs.desc: Charles River has no standing rare-disease grant program but has done case-by-case rare-disease collaborations with foundations and academic groups (humanized model creation for Cure Rare Disease; a CDMO deal with the FOXG1 Research Foundation), plus a periodic Research Models in Drug Discovery Award of free model/CRO support. Discounted tafazzin model work or a manufacturing partnership would go through business development; there is no portal.
programs.eligibility: Foundations and academic groups with a defined preclinical need.
programs.apply: Via the rare-disease contact form on criver.com.

programs.name: Gene therapy partnering routes (Rocket, Forge, Andelyn, AskBio)
programs.desc: No company currently runs an open application program for BTHS gene therapy. Companies with relevant programs: Rocket Pharmaceuticals has three clinical-stage inherited-cardiomyopathy AAV programs (PKP2-ACM, Danon, BAG3-DCM) and has originated programs from academic labs; Forge Biologics has subsidized manufacturing for patient-foundation programs (Progeria Research Foundation) and sits in the NIH Bespoke Gene Therapy Consortium; Andelyn Biosciences and AskBio are academic-adjacent AAV manufacturers. BSF documents the AAV-TAZ preclinical science base; no industry partner has been publicly named.
programs.eligibility: Academic labs and foundations with gene-therapy programs seeking an industry partner or manufacturing.
programs.apply: Engagement runs through business-development outreach and cardiology/gene-therapy congresses rather than portals.

programs.name: Cloud & GPU research credits (AWS, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA)
programs.desc: In-kind compute for genomics and modeling work: AWS Cloud Credit for Research (up to $5,000 for students, no stated cap for faculty/staff; note Free Tier accounts became ineligible Feb 2026), Google Cloud Research Credits (up to $5,000 faculty/postdoc, $1,000/yr PhD students), Microsoft Azure credits (now mostly routed via the NAIRR Pilot's $20M pool), and the NVIDIA Academic Grant Program (up to 30,000 H100 GPU-hours or hardware — relevant for MD simulation of cardiolipin/TAZ or ML on multi-omics).
programs.eligibility: Faculty, research staff, and graduate students at accredited institutions; NVIDIA requires full-time faculty at a PhD-granting institution.
programs.apply: Each program takes rolling applications through its own page — AWS reviews in ~90–120 days, Google in 6–8 weeks.

programs.name: mitoSHARE Registry & industry research venues
programs.desc: mitoSHARE is a global patient-driven mitochondrial disease registry (~1,600 participants; demographics, barriers to care, natural history, trial readiness) with a patient-controlled consent model — BTHS patients are in scope, and researchers can request de-identified data. Related industry-facing venues: the TREAT MITO consortium for pre-competitive collaboration and data/sample access, and the UMDF Clinical Research Pavilion at the annual Mitochondrial Medicine conference, where sponsors recruit sites and investigators.
programs.eligibility: Researchers requesting de-identified/anonymized registry data; consortium and conference participation open to mito investigators.
programs.apply: Data requests via the mitoSHARE page; consortium inquiries via treatmito.org.

programs.name: Uplifting Athletes Young Investigator Draft
programs.sponsor: Uplifting Athletes (backed by Sanofi, Alexion, UCB, Takeda, Jazz)
programs.desc: Unrestricted grants to ~10 early-career rare-disease researchers annually, awarded at an NFL-style draft event at Lincoln Financial Field ($1.42M to 75 researchers to date). Categories include rare genetic disorders and rare muscular & neurological disorders, both of which cover Barth syndrome.
programs.eligibility: Early-career investigators doing collaborative basic bench research on rare disease; US and Canadian institutions represented.
programs.apply: Download the application form from the site and submit to grants@upliftingathletes.org by September 14, 2026, 11:59 PM EDT.

programs.name: Sanofi iAwards
programs.desc: Seed funding plus dedicated Sanofi expertise; ~40% of funded projects advance to multi-year sponsored research agreements. The 2026 call sought innovative therapeutics for neuromuscular and cardio-muscular diseases addressing monogenic disorders via shared pathways including metabolism, a scope that covers BTHS cardiomyopathy/myopathy. Open only to PIs at ~32 partner institutions (Stanford, Harvard, MIT, UCSF, Columbia, Mass General Brigham, and similar).
programs.eligibility: Principal investigators at Sanofi's partner institutions only; partner status can be confirmed through an institution's tech-transfer or research office.
programs.apply: Through your institution's research office when the annual call opens (~April); pre-proposals route via the institution. Contact: SRI-NA@sanofi.com.

programs.name: Sanofi Rare Disease Medical Grants & Investigator Studies
programs.desc: Sanofi's rare-disease medical arm funds fellowships (salary plus research funding at teaching hospitals and medical schools), independent medical education, and sponsorships in rare genetic diseases, plus an investigator-sponsored studies portal.
programs.eligibility: US/Puerto Rico 501(c) organizations and medical/academic institutions — fellowship applications are institutional rather than individual.
programs.apply: Online applications, rolling, with 8–16 week review; ISS proposals via Sanofi's Envision portal.

programs.name: Takeda Investigator Initiated Research
programs.amount: Funding, study product, and/or regulatory right of reference
programs.desc: Supports interventional, non-interventional, and basic-science studies where the investigator or institution is the sponsor. Areas of interest center on rare metabolic diseases (lysosomal storage disorders), rare hematology, and HAE. Mitochondrial disease is not listed; a BTHS proposal would be judged on alignment with the rare-metabolic area.
programs.eligibility: Academic, private, or governmental investigators/institutions acting as study sponsor.
programs.apply: Rolling submissions via Takeda's Envision IIR portal.

programs.name: Astellas ISR & General Research Grants
programs.desc: Mitochondria is one of Astellas' declared primary R&D focus areas (legacy Mitobridge; ASP0367 for primary mitochondrial myopathy; a mitochondrial cell-therapy deal with Minovia), giving mitochondrial-disease ISR proposals a stated area to align with. General Research Grants also fund registries, networks, and reviews.
programs.eligibility: Researchers, physicians, academic institutions, and consortia as study sponsors; compound-specific areas of interest are listed on the portal.
programs.apply: ISR proposals via the external funding pages, rolling (Japan runs an October–November window); General Research Grants via regional grants offices.

programs.name: Boehringer Ingelheim opnMe (open science platform)
programs.amount: Free tool compounds; funded collaboration calls; postdoc grants
programs.desc: Open to scientists globally regardless of institution: well-characterized tool compounds shipped free ('molecules for free'), funded research collaborations around specific BI molecules ('molecules for collaboration'), themed opn2X collaboration calls, and postdoc grants on defined topics. Applicable to BTHS mechanism work needing pharmacological probes.
programs.eligibility: Any scientist worldwide; per-molecule or per-call terms apply.
programs.apply: Order free molecules or submit proposals directly at opnMe.com; deadlines are per-molecule/per-call.

programs.name: BioMarin External Research (investigator-sponsored studies)
programs.desc: Product and funding support for investigator-sponsored clinical studies (phase 1–4 interventional, observational, and real-world evidence) in rare genetic disease. Does not fund animal-model studies, CME, or sponsorships; BTHS-relevant uses are clinical or natural-history-adjacent studies, not bench science.
programs.eligibility: Qualified clinical investigators in rare genetic disease.
programs.apply: Year-round rolling submissions via the External Research page.

programs.name: Alnylam Advocacy for Impact Grants & IIS
programs.deadline: Advocacy grants annual cycle; IIS rolling
programs.desc: Two routes: Advocacy for Impact Grants are global competitive grants for patient advocacy groups solving unmet needs in rare disease communities (an application guide is published), and an investigator-initiated studies program supports research in Alnylam's areas (ATTR amyloidosis, acute hepatic porphyria, PH1). The IIS areas do not cover mitochondrial disease; the advocacy grants are open to any rare-disease community, including BTHS.
programs.eligibility: Advocacy grants: patient advocacy organizations. IIS: physicians, pharmacists, and researchers qualified by training.
programs.apply: Advocacy grants via the annual cycle on Alnylam's site; IIS via the SteepRock platform.

programs.name: Ultragenyx IST Support & Rare Entrepreneur Bootcamp
programs.desc: Ultragenyx has supported 80+ investigator-sponsored trials globally in rare metabolic/genetic disease (funding and drug). Its annual Rare Entrepreneur Bootcamp, run with the EveryLife Foundation, trains patient advocates who fund rare-disease research in drug development, trial design, IP, and pitching.
programs.eligibility: ISTs: qualified investigators aligned with Ultragenyx's rare metabolic/genetic focus. Bootcamp: patient advocates and foundation leaders.
programs.apply: Bootcamp applications via rarebootcamp.com; IST inquiries through Ultragenyx medical affairs (no public portal).

programs.name: Healx Rare Treatment Accelerator
programs.amount: Up to ~$1M in-kind AI drug-discovery resources per project
programs.deadline: Registration of interest — verify current call
programs.desc: AI-driven drug-repurposing partnerships with rare-disease patient groups, academics, and early-stage biotechs, aiming to advance repurposed candidates toward the clinic in ~24 months ($20M committed; prior partners include FAST/Angelman and FARA). BSF would apply as a patient-group partner. The 2026 call cadence could not be verified; current status is posted at healx.ai.
programs.eligibility: Rare-disease patient groups and foundations; expanded to academic groups and biotechs under RTA 2.0.
programs.apply: Register interest via healx.ai.

programs.name: n-Lorem Foundation (free individualized ASO medicines)
programs.amount: Free ASO discovery, development & lifelong supply
programs.desc: Discovers, develops, and supplies individualized antisense oligonucleotide medicines free for life to 'nano-rare' patients (~1–30 patients worldwide sharing a mutation); 240+ patients accepted to date. BTHS overall exceeds nano-rare scale, but n-Lorem counts by specific mutation, so a private TAFAZZIN variant could qualify. ASOs cannot replace lost gene function, so most loss-of-function TAFAZZIN mutations are unsuitable; splice-correction or upregulation strategies for particular variants remain possible via physician inquiry.
programs.eligibility: Applications come from research physicians at tertiary centers experienced with INDs, for fully genomically characterized patients.
programs.apply: Rolling, via the physician application portal.

programs.name: Danaher–IGI Beacon for CRISPR Cures (partnering route)
programs.deadline: No open call — diseases selected internally
programs.desc: A funded UC Berkeley/UCSF center building a scalable platform for CRISPR therapies for rare monogenic diseases (initial targets in inborn errors of immunity). There is no external application mechanism; diseases are chosen internally. The route in is contact with IGI or its clinical collaborators, presenting a monogenic case such as TAFAZZIN.
programs.eligibility: Invited collaborations only.
programs.apply: Outreach to the Innovative Genomics Institute (innovativegenomics.org) or clinical collaborators.

programs.name: Oxford Nanopore Grant Programme
programs.desc: Reduced-cost long-read nanopore sequencing packs for researchers who lack resources to access the technology — useful for resolving structural or deep-intronic TAFAZZIN variants that short reads miss.
programs.eligibility: Researchers lacking resources to access nanopore sequencing.
programs.apply: Quarterly application cycles via nanoporetech.com account pages (search 'Grant Programme').

programs.name: Agilent Early Career Professor Award
programs.deadline: Annual themed cycle — check current topic
programs.desc: Unrestricted award for tenure-track faculty on an annual themed topic aligned to measurement science and instrumentation; some years cover metabolomics or cell analysis, the areas relevant to cardiolipin lipidomics method development. A separate invitation-only Thought Leader Award funds research personnel and instrumentation.
programs.eligibility: Tenure-track faculty within 12 years of PhD/MD; universities may run limited-submission internal competitions.
programs.apply: Applications go through the Agilent university-relations page when the annual topic is posted; institutions may run limited-submission internal competitions first.

programs.name: Anthropic AI for Science — Rare Disease Research Grants
programs.amount: Up to $50,000 in Claude credits over 6 months
programs.deadline: 2026 call closed Aug 2 — watch for future cycles & hackathons
programs.desc: Claude API credits for rare-disease research, announced July 20, 2026, with access to Claude Opus and approved biology models. Two tracks: Basic Science Partnerships — collaboration between clinical researchers, patient organizations, and data scientists to accelerate discovery of disease mechanisms, in partnership with the Monarch Initiative (Mondo Disease Ontology, DisMech mechanistic classification) — and Biotech Partnerships for early-stage companies (regulatory drafting, therapeutic strategy, shared-mechanism basket trials). BTHS-applicable uses include literature synthesis and mechanism-mining for TAFAZZIN/cardiolipin labs and drug-development support for a future BTHS biotech. The inaugural application window closed Aug 2, 2026; Anthropic has signaled future rare disease hackathons and community-building.
programs.eligibility: Academic scientists doing basic rare-disease research, patient organizations partnering with researchers, and early-stage biotechs developing rare-disease treatments.
programs.apply: The 2026 window (closed Aug 2, 2026, 11:59 PM PST) used a short application form linked from the announcement. Future cycles and hackathons would be announced on the same page.

programs.name: Alexion Charitable Foundation — Rare Belonging Grants
programs.desc: Philanthropic grants to nonprofits serving the rare disease community (71 partners in 15 countries to date), with priorities including mental health and wellness, barriers to care, health literacy, diagnostic access, and patient supports. Grants are not tied to Alexion's product areas; any rare disease organization may apply. A global open call is running August 3–21, 2026.
programs.eligibility: Third-party nonprofit organizations serving rare disease communities, globally.
programs.apply: Submit a Preliminary Request Form during the open call after reviewing the ACF Grant Guidelines. Contact: ACF@Alexion.com.

programs.name: Amgen #RAREis Advocate Grant
programs.desc: One-time grants to rare disease patient advocacy organizations for programs and disease education (75 grants awarded in 2024), disease-agnostic within rare disease. In 2026 the program narrows to US-based organizations, which includes BSF. A companion #RAREis Scholarship gives $5,000 to students living with rare diseases.
programs.eligibility: US-based rare disease advocacy organizations (2026).
programs.apply: The annual application window is posted at rareiscommunity.com (the 2026 window was unconfirmed at research time); contact rareconnect@amgen.com.

programs.name: Genentech Corporate Giving & Funding Request System
programs.desc: Charitable contributions and grants across health equity, patient support, and scientific community engagement, through an open online Funding Request System (Genentech maintains relationships with 500+ patient advocacy organizations across 50 disease areas). Therapeutic-area RFPs are posted periodically.
programs.eligibility: IRS-recognized 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) US organizations (or foreign equivalents with W8-BEN), and US governmental organizations.
programs.apply: Submit via the Funding Request System at least 60 days before project start; advocacy sponsorships also flow through the Patient Advocacy Relations team.

programs.name: Pfizer Independent Medical Education & Competitive Grants
programs.desc: Cash grants for independent medical education and quality improvement, with patient advocacy groups explicitly listed as eligible applicants. Grants track posted RFP topics plus a general request channel; rare disease is a Pfizer area, though not BTHS specifically — fit depends on broader cardiomyopathy/rare-disease education RFPs.
programs.eligibility: Patient advocacy groups, medical societies, med-ed companies, and academic institutions; must align with Pfizer therapeutic areas.
programs.apply: Respond to posted RFPs or submit a general IME request through Pfizer's online grant portal.

programs.name: Pharma Education & Sponsorship Portals (Takeda, Sobi, Ipsen, Recordati, Sanofi, Chiesi)
programs.desc: Open-process but therapeutic-area-aligned portals a rare-disease nonprofit can use for education RFPs and sponsorships: Takeda's Support Portal (60+ days lead), Sobi's grants portal (90+ days; hemophilia/immunology-aligned), Ipsen US grants (90+ days; plus Fondation Ipsen's episodic rare-disease mini-grants), Recordati Rare Diseases educational grants, Sanofi US advocacy support, and Chiesi Global Rare Diseases sponsorships. None of these companies has a BTHS-specific area; the portals cover general rare-disease education programs.
programs.eligibility: Nonprofit organizations; requests must generally align with each company's therapeutic areas.
programs.apply: Each portal takes online requests with a letter of request, agenda, budget, and W-9; plan 60–90 days ahead.

programs.name: AWS Imagine Grant
programs.amount: Unrestricted funds up to $200K + AWS credits by tier
programs.desc: Annual competitive grant for US nonprofits using cloud technology, in three tiers: Momentum to Modernize (≤$50K), Go Further Faster (≤$150K), and Pathfinder (≤$200K), each pairing unrestricted funds with AWS credits and technical guidance. Eligible uses include registry or data infrastructure. The 2026–2027 Round One closed June 5, 2026.
programs.eligibility: US 501(c)(3) organizations.
programs.apply: Applications open with the next round (spring 2027) via the AWS Imagine Grant page.

programs.name: Nonprofit Technology Stack (Google, Microsoft, Salesforce, Canva, Slack, TechSoup)
programs.sponsor: Google / Microsoft / Salesforce / Canva / Slack / Asana / TechSoup
programs.desc: In-kind software and advertising programs for nonprofits: Google Ad Grants ($10,000/month in free search ads — requires a 501(c)(3), HTTPS site, and ongoing 5% CTR compliance), Microsoft 365 Business Basic free up to 300 seats plus ~75% discounts and a $2,000/yr Azure credit (free Business Premium was discontinued July 2025), Salesforce Power of Us (10 free Enterprise licenses), Canva Pro free, Slack Pro free under 250 members, Asana at 50% off, and TechSoup's donated/discounted software marketplace (also the validation backbone for several other programs).
programs.eligibility: Verified 501(c)(3) organizations (validation via Percent, Goodstack, or TechSoup depending on program).
programs.apply: Each program has a short online application; TechSoup validation and Google for Nonprofits are the usual starting points.

programs.name: NIH Fellowships & Career Development Awards (F30/F31/F32, K08, K99/R00, T32)
programs.deadline: 3 cycles/yr — F: Apr 8, Aug 8, Dec 8; K: Feb 12, Jun 12, Oct 12
programs.desc: Training and career-development support at every stage: F30/F31 predoctoral and F32 postdoctoral fellowships (stipend, tuition, allowance), K08 for clinician-scientists (salary plus research costs, 3–5 years), and K99/R00 Pathway to Independence (1–2 mentored years then up to 3 independent years, up to $249,000 total costs/yr, portable to a faculty position). No disease restriction; mitochondrial and cardiolipin biology projects are eligible across mechanisms, including F32 and K99 for BTHS postdocs.
programs.eligibility: Career-stage defined: F30/F31 enrolled doctoral students, F32 postdocs, K08 clinicians (MD/DO/MD-PhD), K99 postdocs within 4 years of starting postdoc. F and most K awards require US citizenship or permanent residency; K99/R00 is open to any nationality. T32 slots are applied for through your institution's training program.
programs.apply: Applications go through ASSIST/Grants.gov under the current parent announcements, with the institution's grants office. Standard NIH due dates run three cycles per year. Fellowship review criteria were revised for applications due on or after Jan 25, 2025.

programs.name: Hartwell Individual Biomedical Research Award
programs.desc: Funds early-stage, innovative, translational biomedical research to benefit children of the United States; Barth syndrome's pediatric cardiomyopathy falls within this scope. The foundation favors high-risk projects not yet fundable by NIH. Also funds $100,000/2-year postdoctoral fellowships attached to top award applicants.
programs.eligibility: Nomination only: each year the foundation invites its Top Ten Centers of Biomedical Research (3 nominees each) plus at-large institutions (2 nominees). Nominees must be US citizens with full-time appointments at a participating institution.
programs.apply: Applications route through each institution's internal Hartwell competition, run by its research development / limited-submissions office (internal deadlines are typically spring; CHOP's 2026 internal deadline was June 18). The foundation reviews nominees and announces awards in spring.

programs.name: Child Health Research Awards
programs.deadline: Two cycles/year; September 2026 cycle open now
programs.desc: Hypothesis-driven basic, clinical, public-health, or epidemiological research on child health, aimed at junior investigators; early-career Barth syndrome projects in pediatric cardiomyopathy, neutropenia, or metabolism qualify. Award includes 10% indirects.
programs.eligibility: Geographically restricted to nonprofit academic, medical, and research institutions in the six New England states. Applicants must be within 5 years (PhD) or 7 years (physician-scientist) of completing training. Open application — no nomination needed.
programs.apply: Direct application via the foundation's site; two funding cycles per year (January and September). The September 2026 cycle is open; the exact deadline (typically ~April) is posted on the site.

programs.name: Pediatric Research Grants (Major & Novice Awards)
programs.deadline: Concept papers ~Feb annually; full proposals Jul 15
programs.desc: Health and nutrition research benefiting infants and young children from birth to age 3. Barth-relevant scope: infantile cardiomyopathy and neutropenia diagnosis and management projects. The Novice track (up to $30,000) targets fellows and junior faculty seeking pilot funding.
programs.eligibility: US nonprofit and academic institutions; open application, no nomination. Novice awards target early-career researchers and fellows.
programs.apply: Two-stage process: submit a concept paper (2026 deadline was Feb 2; next cycle ~Dec 2026–Feb 2027), then invited full proposals due July 15 with decisions in late November.

programs.name: Patient-Partnered Collaborations & Rare As One Network
programs.amount: $2,000,000 over 4 years (PPC); 5-year capacity grants (Rare As One)
programs.deadline: Rare As One round 4 opens fall 2026
programs.desc: Two vehicles: Patient-Partnered Collaborations fund teams pairing a patient-led organization with research labs at $2M over 4 years (recent RFAs covered rare neurodegenerative and rare inflammatory pediatric disease). Rare As One gives 5-year capacity-building grants to patient-led rare disease organizations; cycle 3 covered inborn errors of metabolism (BTHS-adjacent), and a fourth round opens fall 2026. Eligibility for a BSF-plus-TAFAZZIN-lab team depends on the disease scope of future RFAs.
programs.eligibility: Rare As One: patient-led advocacy organizations (BSF would be the applicant). Patient-Partnered Collaborations: joint teams of an advocacy organization and academic labs.
programs.apply: RFAs are posted at apply.chanzuckerberg.com when cycles open; the fall 2026 Rare As One round and future PPC disease scopes are the next opportunities.

programs.name: Career Awards at the Scientific Interface (CASI)
programs.desc: Bridges postdoc to faculty for scientists crossing from physical, mathematical, computational, or engineering backgrounds into biology: roughly $100K/yr for 1–2 postdoc years, then $120K/yr for the first 3 faculty years. BTHS-relevant directions include computational lipidomics, cardiolipin membrane biophysics, and modeling of mitochondrial function.
programs.eligibility: PhD in physical/mathematical/computational science or engineering, doing postdoctoral work in biological sciences at a US or Canadian institution. Degree-date windows apply — see the RFP.
programs.apply: LOI-screened annual cycle: submit LOI by August 14, 2026 (3 PM ET); invited full proposals follow.

programs.name: Postdoctoral Enrichment Program (PDEP)
programs.desc: Career-development supplement (not salary) for postdoctoral fellows from underrepresented groups in biomedical research: $10K research supplies plus $10K education/training in years 1–2, and $20K in year 3 toward transition to the professoriate.
programs.eligibility: Postdoctoral fellows from underrepresented groups in biomedical/medical research at US or Canadian degree-granting institutions, with a committed mentor.
programs.apply: Direct application; annual cycle with a ~January deadline (Jan 20, 2026 last cycle — expect similar January 2027).

programs.name: Pew Scholars Program in the Biomedical Sciences
programs.desc: Flexible support for early-career basic biomedical research, awarded on scientific excellence rather than disease area; cardiolipin/mitochondrial biology programs are eligible.
programs.eligibility: Nomination only — one nominee per invited institution, chosen through internal limited-submission competitions. Assistant professors running an independent lab (regular appointment), first appointed no earlier than ~3 years before the cycle; maximum two application attempts.
programs.apply: Nomination runs through each institution's limited-submissions office in spring. For the 2027 class: institutional nominations were due May 13, 2026, nominee applications Sept 3, 2026.

programs.name: Searle Scholars Program
programs.desc: Supports new tenure-track faculty in basic biomedical sciences and chemistry; selection is field-agnostic.
programs.eligibility: Nomination only — invited institutions put forward 1–2 nominees each via internal competition. Must be in your first tenure-track assistant professor appointment (recent-appointment cutoffs apply; check current cycle dates). Basic research focus, not purely clinical.
programs.apply: Institutions run internal competitions in summer; nomination and application are due Sept 30, 2026 for awards beginning July 1, 2027.

programs.name: Beckman Young Investigator Program
programs.desc: Supports young faculty in chemistry and the life sciences, favoring innovative methods and instrumentation. Cardiolipin chemistry, lipidomics method development, or mitochondrial imaging tools fit; clinical research and single-target drug discovery are excluded.
programs.eligibility: Open application (no nomination). Tenure-track faculty within the first 4 years of appointment and ≤10 years post-PhD; US citizens or permanent residents; external funding cap of $225,000 direct annualized at application.
programs.apply: Submit an LOI through the SurveyMonkey Apply portal (annual ~July deadline; 2026 round just closed — next expected July 2027); invited full proposals and finalist interviews follow in spring.

programs.name: Freeman Hrabowski Scholars Program
programs.amount: Up to $8.6M over up to 10 years
programs.desc: Major early-career faculty support (salary plus research budget over up to two 5-year terms), weighing scientific excellence together with inclusive lab leadership and mentoring. From the 2028 competition, this runs combined with the Hanna Gray Fellows program.
programs.eligibility: Tenure-track (or equivalent) faculty at HHMI-eligible US institutions with at most 7 years as a lab head as of Dec 15, 2026; must hold or begin the appointment by May 1, 2028. Open application.
programs.apply: Applications for the combined 2028 competition open November 3, 2026; the applicant guide is already posted.

programs.name: HHMI Investigator Program
programs.desc: "People, not projects": HHMI employs the scientist outright, covering salary and a full research budget in any biomedical field, including mitochondrial biology. Selection targets established PIs with substantial track records.
programs.eligibility: PIs at HHMI-eligible US institutions with roughly 7+ years running an independent lab. Open application from eligible institutions (competitions run about every 5 years).
programs.apply: Online competition — next opens September 28, 2027 with a September 30, 2027 deadline.

programs.name: Vallee Scholars Award
programs.desc: One-time career-development award for basic biomedical research with no restrictions on holding other funding.
programs.eligibility: Nomination only — one nomination from each of ~24 invited elite institutions (Harvard, MIT, Stanford, Oxford, Karolinska, etc.). PhD/MD within 12 years; independent researcher for ≤6 years.
programs.apply: Through your institution's internal competition; nominations close ~December 1 annually.

programs.name: Rita Allen Foundation Scholars
programs.desc: Early-career support restricted to cancer, immunology, neuroscience, or pain. Barth syndrome work qualifies only under a neuroscience or innate-immunity/neutropenia framing.
programs.eligibility: Nomination only — one candidate per selected institution. Independent investigators, preferably within the first 3 years of a tenure-track appointment, at US institutions (citizenship not required). Cannot stack with Beckman/Pew/Searle/Vallee awards starting the same year.
programs.apply: Nomination runs through each institution's limited-submissions process, ~September for the following year's class.

programs.name: Clinical Scientist Development Award
programs.deadline: Unverified — no active cycle found as of Aug 2026
programs.desc: Supports clinical research by junior physician-scientists transitioning to independence ($150K/yr direct plus $15K/yr indirect). Does not support animal work; a BTHS project would need human subjects, such as natural history, cardiac phenotyping, or biomarker studies. No active RFA was verifiable as of August 2026; the last confirmed competition was 2023.
programs.eligibility: MD, MD/PhD, or DO (or foreign equivalent) at assistant professor rank at US degree-granting institutions.
programs.apply: Historically LOI in November followed by full application in March via the foundation's portal. Whether a current cycle exists needs confirmation from the foundation before an application is planned.

programs.name: Wellcome Early-Career, Career Development & Discovery Awards
programs.deadline: Discovery round closes Sept 22, 2026, then always-open
programs.desc: Wellcome funds any health-related science, including rare mitochondrial disease, at three career stages: Early-Career Awards (up to 5 years, full salary plus up to £400,000 expenses), Career Development Awards (mid-career), and Discovery Awards (established teams, average £3.5M, up to 8 years).
programs.eligibility: The administering organization must be in the UK, Republic of Ireland (Early-Career), or eligible countries — nationality is open but the lab must be there. From 29 October 2026, Discovery Award lead applicants are restricted to the UK and LMICs in Africa / South & South-east Asia; US-based investigators can participate only as co-applicants.
programs.apply: Applications go through the Wellcome Funding online system. The current Discovery round closes September 22, 2026, after which the scheme becomes always-open with no deadlines. The next Early-Career round is posted on the site.

programs.name: ERC Starting, Consolidator & Advanced Grants
programs.desc: Investigator-driven frontier research in any field. Starting (2–7 yrs post-PhD, up to €1.5M/5 yrs), Consolidator (7–12 yrs, up to €2M), Advanced (established leaders, up to €2.5M). Relevant to European Barth syndrome labs working on tafazzin and cardiolipin.
programs.eligibility: Any nationality, but the host institution must be in an EU member state or Horizon-associated country and the PI must spend at least 50% of their time in Europe.
programs.apply: Via the EU Funding & Tenders portal. ERC-2027-StG opens Jul 22, 2026 (deadline Oct 14, 2026); ERC-2027-CoG opens Sep 24, 2026 (deadline Jan 12, 2027); ERC-2027-AdG opens May 27, 2027 (deadline Aug 26, 2027).

programs.name: HFSP Research Grants & Postdoctoral Fellowships
programs.desc: Funds international, interdisciplinary teams of 2–4 PIs doing basic 'frontier' life science (no applied, clinical, or drug-development work), plus postdoctoral fellowships requiring an international move. A mechanistic cardiolipin-biophysics collaboration — for example a US biologist with an EU physicist — qualifies; a translational BTHS therapy project does not.
programs.eligibility: Research Grants: independent lab heads anywhere, with at least one member in an HFSP member country; teams should be intercontinental with no substantial prior joint publications. Early Career variant: all members ≤5 yrs independent and ≤10 yrs post-PhD. Fellowships: PhDs changing fields and countries.
programs.apply: Two-stage via ProposalCentral: LOIs initiate ~mid-March annually (grants) and ~May (fellowships); invited full proposals in September; awards the following March.

programs.name: Experiment.com Science Crowdfunding
programs.desc: All-or-nothing crowdfunding for small research projects (~48% success rate; junior investigators outperform senior ones). Typical uses are pilot data and trainee side-projects; rare-disease campaigns benefit from an engaged patient community, and BSF's network can amplify a campaign. Amounts are small relative to grant funding.
programs.eligibility: Any researcher; projects are reviewed for scientific clarity and feasibility before going live. No institutional restriction.
programs.apply: Projects are created at experiment.com — free to start; 8% platform fee plus ~3–5% payment processing on successfully funded projects only.

programs.name: RARE Impact Grants (for advocacy organizations)
programs.desc: Grants to patient advocacy organizations in Global Genes' Global Advocacy Alliance for education, patient support, and research-advocacy capacity. Not investigator-initiated science — relevant to the Barth Syndrome Foundation as an organization rather than to individual labs.
programs.eligibility: Rare-disease patient advocacy organizations that are members of the Global Advocacy Alliance.
programs.apply: Via the Global Genes prospectus/application when cycles open.

programs.name: EveryLife Foundation Programs (advocacy & policy)
programs.desc: Policy and regulatory advocacy support rather than bench research: the Rare Giving program funds advocacy groups and patient advocates (travel, survey tools, IRB and publication fees for patient-experience data), and #RAREis Scholarships support students living with rare diseases. Applies to BSF policy work such as newborn screening, not to lab funding.
programs.eligibility: Advocacy organizations and patients, not scientists.
programs.apply: Through the program pages at everylifefoundation.org.
